channel.title: Scarlett Hao. · What's new
channel.description: What's shipped on scarletthao.me: new stories, features and small fun things, newest first.

item.title: Base camps (Functionality)
item.description:
• Every flight card leads with the number that matters most: Polaris seats open on international flights, all open seats on domestic.
  • Standby Radar can plan from a second home airport for part of the year, switching on its own by month or by hand.
  • Trips without a nonstop now count the connection through a United hub, as full as its fuller leg.

item.title: Good time to go (New)
item.description:
• Standby Radar suggests places that are in season and whose flights usually run emptier than most, like ski season in Jackson Hole or whale season in Cabo. Somewhere empty only because it’s off season never makes the list.
  • Pick a month to see more, or use “Places in season with room” when your dates are set.

item.title: A calendar for standby (New)
item.description:
• Standby Radar has a six-week calendar. Days you’ve checked are green, yellow or red, days that look open are outlined, and tapping a day shows its flights.
  • With set dates, Roll the dice lays out each place a few days either side, so you can see where and when is most open.

item.title: Standby Radar remembers every flight (Functionality)
item.description:
• Every flight in a screenshot now saves to the log on its own, and fixes save as you type.
  • Flights with good odds stay on the home screen, with how their seats have moved since the first check.
  • Check the same flight a few times and it learns the route’s pattern, like seats that start open and fill up the week of departure.
  • Everyone starts with a blank slate: places and tracked flights stay on the phone that added them.

item.title: Standby Radar (New)
item.description:
• A new trip planner under Play, our nudge to fly standby once a month. It shows which of our favorite places look open and when, using public route history.
  • On the day, upload a screenshot of the seat counts and it tells you your odds.

item.title: Follow along, and a guide for AI (Functionality)
item.description:
• This changelog now has an RSS feed, so you can follow new stories and features in any feed reader.
  • A short llms.txt guide helps AI assistants describe me and my work accurately, and link back to the right pages.

item.title: Weekend mode (Fun)
item.description: • On Saturdays and Sundays, the line under my name knows it’s the weekend. Weekend mode: touching grass.

item.title: The second full story: Creating value propositions to buy direct (New)
item.description: • The direct-to-consumer story now has its own page: how Keurig, Royal Caribbean, Juul, Equilibria and Tatcha gave customers a reason to buy direct, and took it around the world. Find it from the Experience section.

item.title: Résumé on request (New)
item.description:
• A new Résumé link in the Contact section. Click it to send me a quick note, and I’ll email it to you. Takes 2 minutes!
  • scarletthao.me/resume goes straight there.

item.title: Token count (Fun)
item.description: • The footer now shows roughly how many AI tokens it has taken to build this site: 10M+ and counting.

item.title: Easier to read (Functionality)
item.description:
• Paragraphs no longer end with a single word hanging on its own line.
  • The headline on the home page breaks in a cleaner place, on laptops and phones.
  • The small tags (like these ones) and the “Work in progress” label are a little bigger and easier to read.
  • The banner’s close button now lines up with the right edge of the page.

item.title: Banner lines up with the page (Functionality)
item.description: • The daily banner now starts at the same left edge as my name and the page, instead of floating in the middle.

item.title: Easier to find (Functionality)
item.description:
• Search engines now get a clear profile of who I am, with links to my LinkedIn, Substack and GitHub, so searching my name finds this site.
  • A clearer page title, and “Hi, I’m Scarlett” is now the page’s main heading.
  • The preview card for sharing the site has the new photo.

item.title: A new headshot (New)
item.description: • A new, sunnier photo in the intro, shown as a taller portrait instead of a circle.

item.title: Fun fact of the day (Fun)
item.description:
• On days without a holiday, a “Did you know?” fact shows up under the header. Everyone gets the same one, and it changes every day.
  • 98 facts to start, about animals, food, space, history, places, words and sports, plus a few about Vespas, chips and San Francisco.

item.title: The first full story: Crossing the Valley of Death (New)
item.description:
• The Defense Digital Service story now has its own page: how a dual-use drone program went from proof of concept to a dependable product with a long-term home in the U.S. Navy. Find it from the Experience section.
  • A new story-page design, before and after, that the Kodiak and direct-to-consumer stories will use too.

item.title: hello@scarletthao.me (Functionality)
item.description: • A new email address on the site's own domain: hello@scarletthao.me, in the Contact section.

item.title: Brand logos (New)
item.description: • The direct-to-consumer story now shows the six brands I worked with: Keurig, Royal Caribbean, Juul Labs, Tatcha, Equilibria, and Plant People.

item.title: Filter by tag (Functionality)
item.description: • Click a tag, in the key or on any update, to see only those updates. Click it again to see everything.

item.title: One header, everywhere (Functionality)
item.description:
• The same header on every page: name, San Francisco time and weather, and the menu. It stays at the top as you scroll.
  • Your name and the menu now share one line on every screen. The San Francisco time sits underneath and tucks away when you scroll. On phones, Experience is shortened to Work.

item.title: Brain Power (Fun)
item.description:
• A trivia board: pick a category and a point value, answer the clue, win or lose the points.
  • Three modes: Feel smart (what you know), Get smart (what you want to learn), and Wild card. Set your own categories, too.
  • Both side projects now live at /play.

item.title: Holiday banners (Fun)
item.description:
• On holidays, a small banner with one line sits above the header. Starting today: Happy Veterans Day, and thank you to everyone who served.
  • About twenty days a year, from New Year’s to Vespa’s birthday. Close it and it stays closed.
  • The banner sits just below the header and scrolls away with the page.

item.title: Easier to read, easier to navigate (Functionality)
item.description:
• Small gray text is a touch darker, so it’s readable for everyone.
  • A “Skip to content” link for keyboard users, on every page.
  • Snacky Vespa’s “Roll again” button is easier to read in dark mode.
  • Checked against WCAG 2.2 AA, the web accessibility standard: contrast, keyboard navigation, and 200% zoom.

item.title: Experience, told as stories (New)
item.description:
• The three experience cards now lead with the story: building a business off of autonomy, crossing the Valley of Death, and why people buy direct (and come back).
  • Each card links to a full story. Those are still being written, so for now the links land on a coming-soon page with a little road-work sign.
  • On wider screens the cards now stretch beyond the text column, so the photos get more room.

item.title: Footer credits (Functionality)
item.description:
• The footer now names everything the site runs on, including Umami for cookie-free visit counts.
  • Snacky Vespa credits openrouteservice and OpenStreetMap for its routes.

item.title: Snacky Vespa on real streets (Functionality)
item.description:
• Loops now follow real streets with freeways off: no 101 or 280. Times and miles come from the actual route.
  • Stops you walk into, like Lands End or the Wave Organ, route to a nearby place to park.

item.title: Snacky Vespa usage stats (Functionality)
item.description: • Anonymous counts of which snacks, moods, and times people pick, how many loops they roll, and how many open in Google Maps. No cookies, no locations.

item.title: Snacky Vespa (Fun)
item.description:
• A new ride planner: pick a snack, a start time, and how long you’ve got. It plans a loop through San Francisco around Sunday’s weather, with curious stops and a snack somewhere new.
  • Chase the sun, or go visit Karl the Fog. Every roll is a different loop.

item.title: Short links (Functionality)
item.description: • Easy-to-share addresses: scarletthao.me/linkedin, /substack, /github, and /x.

item.title: Light and dark toggle (New)
item.description: • A small sun/moon button in the header switches between light and dark. The site remembers your choice; until you pick, it follows your device.

item.title: Spring cleaning (Functionality)
item.description:
• Reorganized the site’s files: images in one folder, and shared styles and scripts used by every page.
  • Added a friendly 404 page, a sitemap, and a public README.

item.title: GitHub link (New)
item.description: • Added my GitHub to the contact links, between Substack and X.

item.title: Link preview (Functionality)
item.description: • Sharing scarletthao.me on LinkedIn, iMessage, or Slack now shows a branded preview card with my headline, headshot, and the little truck.

item.title: San Francisco weather (Fun)
item.description: • The line under my name now includes the current SF weather, like “58° and foggy.” Powered by Open-Meteo.

item.title: Changelog tags (Functionality)
item.description: • Every entry is now tagged New, Fun, or Functionality, with a key at the top.

item.title: Footer colophon (New)
item.description:
• Added a short note on how the site is made: words are mine; built with Claude Code, hosted on GitHub, tracked in Linear.
  • Hid the résumé link until the PDF is ready.

item.title: Photos on the experience cards (New)
item.description: • Each experience card now has a visual beside the story: a Permian Basin truck for Kodiak, a drone for DDS, and the brands I worked with for direct-to-consumer.

item.title: Favicon (New)
item.description: • Added a site icon (an “S” with a red dot) for browser tabs and phone home screens.

item.title: Driverless truck (Fun)
item.description:
• A tiny driverless truck with a confetti trailer now drives along a yellow lane line at the bottom of the screen as you scroll. Scroll up and it turns around.
  • Now drives on every page, including this one.

item.title: Real logos (New)
item.description: • Swapped the letter placeholders on the experience cards for the Kodiak and Defense Digital Service logos.

item.title: Local time (Fun)
item.description: • Added my live San Francisco time under my name, with a note on what I’m probably up to.

item.title: Analytics (Functionality)
item.description:
• Added privacy-friendly analytics (Umami). No cookies, no tracking across sites.
  • Counting clicks on Copy email, LinkedIn, Substack, and X to see what people do after reading.

item.title: New site (New)
item.description:
• Moved off Squarespace to a hand-built site, made with Claude Code and hosted on GitHub.
  • Rewrote the story around scaling, in reality: who I am, the patterns I’ve found, and how I organize chaos.
  • Added experience cards with impact numbers, and a section on where I can help.
  • Works in light and dark mode, on phones and desktops.
